notes:
Summary: Closed-lost (competed primarily against Together + Replicate pilots). Primary decision: internal infra + pricing with competitor + exec freeze.

Deal history & timeline:
- 2025-09-02: Initial inbound via events form (interest in low-latency reranking and embedding store). AE assigned (Maya).
- 2025-09-18: Discovery call w/ ML Eng lead (Priya) — clarified throughput: 200 qps for reranking + 1000 embeddings/day. Cost sensitivity flagged.
- 2025-10-02: Demo of hosted API + dedicated flow. SE (Carlos) ran latency benchmarks vs their sample data. Notes: 65ms median token latency on our dedicated config.
- 2025-11-06: POC kickoff. Provided sandbox dedicated cluster quote and integration guide. Jira ticket INF-3421 created for auth/kms questions.
- 2025-12-15: Security review — requested SAML SSO, audit logs, and key management details. Submitted security deck (/drive/security/lynx/security-questions-response.docx).
- 2026-01-12: Mid-POC sync. Fireflies transcript FF-2026-01-12-8932. CTO quote: "We like Redwood perf but worried about vendor lock + long-term cost predictability."
- 2026-01-28: Procurement asks for on-prem/air-gap option; our Private offering timeline too long for their roadmaps.
- 2026-02-03: Competitor demos (Together + Replicate) — Together proposed hybrid self-managed + managed control plane; Replicate offered simplified model registry + cheaper inference for the exact model family they wanted.
- 2026-02-04: Procurement informs AE that they will select competitor and pause budget until fiscal reorg.

Win/loss analysis (notes):
- Lost to Together on long-term flexibility: their hybrid approach aligned with Lynx infra roadmap and gave engineering team comfort (self-hosted pieces, clear OSS path).
- Replicate won on immediate cost-per-token and ease of onboarding for the community models they needed.
- Internal blockers: no single executive champion; ML infra lead favored self-manage while Product prioritized predictable SaaS. Procurement eventually locked to cheaper/hybrid vendor.
- Security: SSO and SOC2 were table-stakes; main security ask was KMS residency and audit retention which we can do but timeline was slower than competitor's proposed timeline.
- Pricing: initial committed pricing looked competitive, but total cost of ownership favoring Together for on-prem amortized infra 3-year model was persuasive.

Action items / next steps recorded:
- Postmortem scheduled with AE/SE/RevOps on 2026-02-18 to capture lessons and update battlecard.
- Send competitive brief (Together/Replicate) to Sales and Solutions — include POC feedback and sample TCO model (owner: Carlos).
- Keep in cadence: reach back in 6 months for fiscal-cycle check; add to account watchlist for private offering readiness.
